<section class="sisterhood-group philanthropy-group" aria-labelledby="girls-on-the-run">
<h3 id="girls-on-the-run">Giving Back Through Philanthropy</h3>
<div class="sisterhood-story">
<p>One of my favorite parts of being a member of Gamma Phi was the opportunity to participate in our philanthropy and give back to the community. Gamma Phi’s philanthropy is Girls on the Run, an after-school program that helps young girls build confidence, develop healthy habits, and recognize their potential.</p>
<p>Throughout the year, our chapter hosted a variety of fundraising events to support Girls on the Run. We sold ice cream, hosted pumpkin-carving events, held karaoke nights, and organized other activities that brought our community together. All of the funds raised through these events were donated to Girls on the Run.</p>
<p>Members of our chapter also had the opportunity to serve as coaches for the girls in the program. While I was not able to be a coach myself, I always looked for opportunities to help with activities, support practices, and participate in the girls’ practice 5K.</p>
<p>Twice a year, Girls on the Run hosts a 5K for their program, and our entire chapter volunteers at the event. There are many ways to get involved, from checking participants in to helping the girls with their hair and accessories, or my personal favorite, being a cheerleader for the girls. We would spread out along different points of the 5K course and cheer on the girls as they ran by. It was so cute watching all their faces light up. I am incredibly grateful for the opportunities Gamma Phi has given me to be involved in Girls on the Run.</p>
</div>

<section class="sisterhood-group" aria-labelledby="big-little">
<h3 id="big-little">Big / Little - Memories through the years</h3>
<div class="sisterhood-story">
<p>Another fun part of being in a sorority is getting to participate in Big/Little. As a sophomore, you get to be paired with a new freshman member as their “Big.” The week leading up to the Big/Little reveal is filled with surprises, gifts, and Gamma Phi merchandise as you get to learn more about each other and make them feel welcomed and excited to be part of the chapter.</p>
<p>Being a Big means you become a mentor and someone your Little can turn to as they adjust to college life. Bigs help their Littles become familiar with campus and learn Gamma Phi traditions and expectations. I really enjoyed being someone my Little could rely on and making her transition into college a little easier.</p>
<p>One of my favorite things to do with my Little is go on coffee and study dates. Whether we are catching up over coffee or working on assignments together, I am so grateful to have built a friendship that means so much to me.</p>
</div>
